questions.section: Managed Gen AI Evaluation, Autoraters & Agent Simulation
questions.question: A financial services agent passes 97% of pre-release evaluation cases when scored solely on `FINAL_RESPONSE_QUALITY`, yet a compliance audit reveals that in 14% of approved refunds the agent skipped calling `check_aml_watchlist` and `verify_refund_policy` before executing `issue_refund`. What evaluation blind spot occurred, and which Gen AI Evaluation configuration closes it?

options.text: Raise the `FINAL_RESPONSE_QUALITY` pass threshold from 0.90 to 0.99 and switch the autorater temperature from 0.0 to 0.7.
options.why_wrong: Outcome-only text judges inspect the politeness and clarity of the final message, not whether intermediate compliance tools were invoked first.

options.text: Outcome-only 'right answer, wrong path' blind spot; add `trajectory_in_order_match` plus `HALLUCINATION` and forbidden-tool checks.
Replace all evaluation metrics with `BLEU` and `ROUGE-L` lexical n-gram overlap against a single reference paragraph written by compliance.
options.why_wrong: Lexical n-gram overlap on final prose has zero visibility into tool-call trajectories and penalizes valid paraphrasing.

options.text: Assert `trajectory_exact_match` across every read-only search and formatting helper so any extra lookup fails the build.
options.why_wrong: `trajectory_exact_match` is overly brittle when optional read-only lookups vary; `trajectory_in_order_match` enforces mandatory safety ordering without penalizing valid extra reads.

questions.explanation: Outcome-only evaluation suffers from the 'right answer, wrong path' blind spot: an agent can generate a convincing refund confirmation while skipping mandatory compliance checks. Pairing outcome autoraters (`FINAL_RESPONSE_QUALITY`, `HALLUCINATION`) with process/trajectory evaluation—specifically `trajectory_in_order_match` to enforce chronological ordering (`verify_identity -> check_aml_watchlist -> verify_refund_policy -> issue_refund`) and a Tier 1 check for forbidden tools—catches skipped safety gates without breaking when optional read-only lookups occur.
questions.key_takeaway: Eliminate 'right answer, wrong path' blind spots by pairing outcome autoraters with `trajectory_in_order_match` for required safety milestones.

questions.section: Managed Gen AI Evaluation, Autoraters & Agent Simulation
questions.question: An engineering team is preparing to launch a brand-new airline rebooking agent. Because the service has not launched yet, they have zero historical chat logs, and security policy prohibits running load or fault-injection tests against the live passenger reservation mainframe. How should they evaluate multi-turn edge cases and HTTP `503` reservation API brownouts before launch?

options.text: Deploy directly to 100% of production traffic for 48 hours with Online Evaluation Monitors enabled so real passengers generate the initial failure dataset.
options.why_wrong: Using live customers as an untested fault-injection harness violates progressive delivery and risks corrupting real reservations.

options.text: Run 2-Step Agent Simulation from an Agent Registry snapshot paired with Environment Simulation to mock tools and inject `503` faults.
Run Shadow Mode on an unrelated FAQ chatbot's traffic while pointing the rebooking agent's write tools at the live passenger mainframe.
options.why_wrong: Shadow mode cannot simulate multi-turn interactive dialogue on an unlaunched product, and live write tools must never execute in shadow mode.

options.text: Use the Zero-Shot Prompt Optimizer alone as a release gate since it mathematically guarantees 100% tool-error recovery without running trajectories.
options.why_wrong: Zero-Shot Optimizer improves static prompt phrasing without executing multi-turn trajectories or testing `503` fault handling.

questions.explanation: Gen AI Evaluation Service provides 2-Step Agent Simulation for cold-start multi-turn testing: Step 1 generates diverse synthetic user scenarios and adversarial personas from an Agent Registry snapshot (prompts, tools, policies), and Step 2 runs multi-turn conversations between an LLM User Simulator and the candidate agent. Pairing this with Environment Simulation replaces live external backends with realistic mocked state and deterministic fault injection (`503`, `429`, malformed JSON).
questions.key_takeaway: When historical logs are missing or live backends are off-limits, combine 2-Step Agent Simulation with Environment Simulation fault injection.

questions.section: Managed Gen AI Evaluation, Autoraters & Agent Simulation
questions.question: You need to evaluate an enterprise research agent across 800 diverse prompts—ranging from SQL debugging to executive memo drafting—where writing a static reference answer for every prompt is impractical, yet a generic 1–5 holistic score fails to catch missing prompt-specific constraints. Which Gen AI Evaluation Service autorater paradigm fits best?

options.text: Adaptive Rubrics, which dynamically generate prompt-specific binary pass/fail tests per query and aggregate weighted verdicts.
Computation-based `exact_match` against an empty reference string so every non-empty completion receives a deterministic binary score.
options.why_wrong: `exact_match` cannot grade open-ended synthesis without a single canonical string, and comparing against an empty string fails valid answers.

options.text: Static Rubrics configured with a single 1–100 integer prompt ('Rate overall helpfulness from 1 to 100') shared across all 800 prompts.
options.why_wrong: Unanchored 1–100 holistic scales suffer from severe mid-scale clustering and miss query-specific constraints.

options.text: Self-grading inside the research agent's own system prompt by asking `gemini-4-argon` to append `<self_score>5/5</self_score>` at the end of every memo.
options.why_wrong: In-session self-grading suffers from self-preference bias and shares the exact same blind spots that produced the response.

questions.explanation: Adaptive Rubrics (`FINAL_RESPONSE_QUALITY`, `GENERAL_QUALITY`, `INSTRUCTION_FOLLOWING`) solve heterogeneous, reference-free evaluation by dynamically generating tailored binary pass/fail rubric items for each individual prompt (for example, checking SQL syntax on query #1 and executive tone + bullet limits on query #2) and aggregating the binary verdicts transparently.
questions.key_takeaway: Use Adaptive Rubrics for reference-free open-ended evaluation across diverse prompts where each query implies distinct pass/fail constraints.

questions.question: In Agent Registry's Observability dashboard, your domain Q&A agent shows clean HTTP 200 status codes and sub-second latency, but `HALLUCINATION` online monitor alerts jumped from 2% to 19% after 12 new MCP tools were added. The `Tools` tab reveals a surge in 'no-tool interactions' on questions that require database lookups. What is the root cause and fix?

options.text: Regional compute pool exhaustion (`Region temporarily at capacity`); file a Gemini TPM quota increase ticket and add 5 SDK retries.
options.why_wrong: HTTP 200 responses are succeeding in under a second; there is no capacity error or HTTP 429 rate limiting.

options.text: Ambiguous or overlapping tool schemas caused the model to skip tools and guess; sharpen tool docstrings and enforce `trajectory_in_order_match`.
Enable `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true` on public Cloud Logging buckets without SDP templates so users can inspect raw prompts.
options.why_wrong: Logging unredacted user prompts to broad buckets leaks PII and does nothing to fix tool-selection confusion.

options.text: Disable Dual-Attribution Audit Logging (`is_agentic=true`) so the SPIFFE agent identity stops conflicting with the human user principal.
options.why_wrong: Dual-attribution audit logs record actor provenance for security forensics and do not prevent the LLM from emitting tool calls.

questions.explanation: In Agent Registry Observability, a spike in 'no-tool interactions' paired with rising `HALLUCINATION` scores indicates Ignored Tools: adding 12 overlapping or poorly described MCP schemas confused tool selection, causing the model to answer from parametric memory instead of querying the database. Remediate by sharpening tool descriptions/boundaries (or scoping tools per sub-agent) and gating releases on `trajectory_in_order_match`.
questions.key_takeaway: High 'no-tool interactions' + rising hallucinations diagnose Ignored Tools from ambiguous schemas; sharpen tool descriptions and gate trajectories.

questions.section: LM Feedback Flywheel, Failure Clustering & Agent Optimizer
questions.question: Your team wants to migrate a complex 3,800-token orchestrator prompt from a frontier model to `gemini-3.8-flash` to cut inference spend by 65%, while also fixing two recurring error patterns discovered in last month's SDP-scrubbed production traces. Manual prompt edits keep breaking older behaviors. Which workflow solves this systematically?

options.text: Run Zero-Shot Optimizer with zero examples and deploy directly to 100% of production without a held-out validation dataset.
options.why_wrong: Zero-Shot Optimizer does not use scored trace data, target-model evaluation loops, or failure clusters, and skipping a held-out split risks regressions.

options.text: Append every single failing user transcript verbatim into the static system prompt until the prompt exceeds 150,000 tokens.
options.why_wrong: Stuffing raw transcripts bloats latency and cost, causes context rot, and overfits to specific historical phrasing.

options.text: Group traces via Failure Cluster Analysis, reserve a held-out split, and run Data-Driven Optimizer (`instruction_and_demo`) targeting `gemini-3.8-flash`.
Point the production traffic router at a floating `-latest` alias and disable `agents-cli eval run` so CI pipelines stop failing on prompt diffs.
options.why_wrong: Floating aliases introduce Model Drift, and disabling CI evaluation gates guarantees silent regressions reach users.

questions.explanation: Data-Driven Prompt Optimizer (`Agent Optimizer`) automates model migrations and cluster remediation by running an iterative closed loop (`evaluate -> analyze failure clusters -> mutate instructions/demos -> re-evaluate on target model`) across `instruction`, `demonstration` (populating Example Store), or `instruction_and_demo` modes. Keeping a held-out validation split hidden from the optimizer verifies true generalization rather than prompt memorization.
questions.key_takeaway: Use Failure Cluster Analysis + Data-Driven Optimizer (`instruction_and_demo`) with a held-out validation split for model migrations and regression-free fixes.

questions.section: Deployment Runtime Selection: Agent Runtime vs. Cloud Run vs. GKE
questions.question: An enterprise architect must choose Google Cloud runtimes for three components: (1) a stateful Python ADK orchestrator requiring managed Sessions and Memory Bank with minimal ops; (2) a custom TypeScript Streamable HTTP MCP server that scales to zero; and (3) serving fine-tuned open-weight `Gemma 4` on L4 GPUs alongside untrusted multi-tenant code sandboxes. Which mapping follows Rule 0?

options.text: (1) Agent Runtime, (2) Cloud Run, (3) GKE with GPU node pools and Agent Sandbox (`gVisor` + `SandboxWarmPool`).
(1) Agent Runtime, (2) Agent Runtime hosting the standalone TypeScript MCP server, (3) Agent Runtime self-hosting `gemini-4-argon` weights on GPUs.
options.why_wrong: Agent Runtime does not host standalone MCP servers or custom GPU model weights, and proprietary `gemini-4-argon` weights cannot be self-hosted anywhere.

options.text: (1) Cloud Run storing session history in local container RAM, (2) GKE bare-metal StatefulSets, (3) Cloud Functions v1 without accelerators.
options.why_wrong: Cloud Run local RAM is wiped on scale-to-zero recycles, GKE adds unnecessary ops for a simple serverless MCP server, and Cloud Functions cannot serve GPU LLMs.

options.text: (1) Managed Agents API hosting custom C++ GPU kernels, (2) BigQuery Stored Procedures, (3) Cloud Workstations with public IPs for prod traffic.
options.why_wrong: Managed Agents API does not host custom GPU kernels, BigQuery is not an HTTP MCP server runtime, and Cloud Workstations are developer IDEs, not production runtimes.

questions.explanation: Following Rule 0 (Managed by Default): (1) Agent Runtime provides the lowest operational overhead for stateful Python/ADK orchestrators with built-in Sessions, Memory Bank, and Example Store; (2) Cloud Run is the primary serverless runtime for custom Streamable HTTP MCP servers and polyglot services (since Agent Runtime does not host standalone MCP servers); and (3) GKE is required when self-hosting open-weight models (`Gemma 4`) on GPUs/TPUs and isolating untrusted code in pre-warmed `gVisor` pods via Agent Sandbox on GKE.
questions.key_takeaway: Map stateful ADK orchestrators to Agent Runtime, custom HTTP MCP servers to Cloud Run, and open-weight GPU serving + gVisor sandboxes to GKE.

questions.section: Deployment Runtime Selection: Agent Runtime vs. Cloud Run vs. GKE
questions.question: During launch week, two incidents occur: (A) deploying a new Agent Runtime instance in `us-central1` fails with `"Region temporarily at capacity"`; and (B) your nightly 20,000-row offline evaluation job ignores your newly purchased Provisioned Throughput (GSUs) and incurs PayGo charges. What explains both behaviors and resolves them?

options.text: (A) Missing `roles/owner` IAM binding on the service account; (B) GSUs only cover Batch Prediction when `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` is overridden at runtime.
options.why_wrong: `Region temporarily at capacity` is physical compute exhaustion (not IAM), GSUs never cover Batch Prediction, and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` is a reserved variable that must not be overridden.

options.text: (A) Physical regional compute exhaustion—deploy to an alternate region or right-size resources; (B) GSUs exclude Batch Prediction—use Batch/Flex ~50% pricing for nightly evals.
(A) Gemini TPM quota limit—file a quota ticket and wait in `us-central1`; (B) Prefix `GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE_BATCH=true` to force Batch onto GSUs.
options.why_wrong: Quota tickets do not add physical compute hardware to an exhausted region, custom `GOOGLE_CLOUD_AGENT_ENGINE*` env vars are reserved/prohibited, and GSUs do not cover Batch.

options.text: (A) Invalid `thinking_level` enum on `gemini-4-argon`; (B) Provisioned Throughput requires disabling implicit caching via explicit `cachedContents` on `gemini-4-argon`.
options.why_wrong: Model parameter errors return HTTP 400 at inference time (not deployment capacity errors), and `gemini-4-argon` supports automatic implicit caching rather than explicit `cachedContents`.

questions.explanation: `"Region temporarily at capacity"` during Agent Runtime deployment indicates physical regional compute pool exhaustion rather than a project quota or IAM issue—resolve it by deploying to an alternate supported region, right-sizing vCPU/RAM, or retrying off-peak. Separately, Provisioned Throughput (GSUs) reserves real-time serving capacity and explicitly does NOT cover Batch Prediction or internal calls made by other managed services (like Agent Search); run nightly offline evals on Batch Prediction / Flex PayGo (~50% discount) and keep GSUs for steady real-time traffic.
questions.key_takeaway: `Region temporarily at capacity` requires region failover/right-sizing (not a quota ticket), and Provisioned Throughput (GSUs) never covers Batch Prediction.
